context_prefix_rationale: TSK_FNDN_* is consumed by SF_FOUNDATION_EXT_NC_v1 (24 tasks). Using FNRP_ (FouNdation RePaint) eliminates all ID collisions. Verified: TSK_FNRP_* has zero existing usage. Pattern follows established convention: FN = foundation, RP = repaint. FNRP prefix is unique across all context_prefixes_in_use.
scope_summary: Combined condition assessment + prep + prime + finish repaint spec for previously painted above-grade foundation walls (poured concrete and CMU). Covers 4-point condition assessment (visual, chalk, adhesion, moisture MC <= 4% HARD STOP), efflorescence treatment, pressure wash (1,500-2,500 PSI), crack patching (cosmetic < 1/8 inch), state-driven primer (chalk-binding for SS_EXT_CHALKING, alkali-resistant spot prime on exposed bare masonry pH 12-14, acrylic stain-block for general RP adhesion), finish coat application (brush_roll primary for small areas, spray_backroll for larger runs). SF-based with ITM_FOUNDATION_WALL. 2 foundation types (poured/CMU). QT2-QT3 only (utilitarian surface — QT4/QT5 excluded). Flat sheen only. No access modifier (ground-level). NEVER caulk the grade-line gap. Simplest exterior RP spec.

relevant_findings.topic: Foundation RP inherits NC moisture strictness — MC <= 4% hard stop
relevant_findings.finding: Foundation moisture threshold remains 4% for RP (same as NC), stricter than masonry wall RP (12%). Foundation has continuous ground contact with capillary moisture rise. MC > 4% = HARD STOP regardless of condition state. Electronic moisture meter at multiple points along foundation band. This is the tightest MC threshold in the entire spec system.

relevant_findings.topic: Grade-line gap NEVER caulked — critical prohibition carries into RP
relevant_findings.finding: The 3/8-inch siding-to-foundation gap with Z-flashing is an intentional drainage plane. NEVER caulk this gap in NC or RP context. Caulking seals the drainage path, trapping moisture behind siding — causes catastrophic rot, mold, and structural damage. During RP, the gap may have been incorrectly caulked by a previous painter — assess and flag for removal if caulked. Mask the gap during painting. #1 grade-line failure mode.

relevant_findings.topic: Four exterior RP substrate states apply to foundation
relevant_findings.finding: Exterior RP uses 4 substrate states: SS_EXT_SOUND_PAINT (existing coating well-adhered — scuff sand, skip prime possible with verified adhesion), SS_EXT_CHALKING (UV degradation — chalk-binding primer required, full surface), SS_EXT_FAILING_PAINT (cracking/peeling localized — pressure wash loose areas, spot prime), SS_EXT_PEELING (widespread failure — heavy wash, full scrape, alkali-resistant primer on exposed bare masonry at pH 12-14, full prime). Condition scale mapping: GOOD=SS_EXT_SOUND_PAINT (1.0x prep), FAIR=SS_EXT_CHALKING or localized SS_EXT_FAILING_PAINT (1.3x prep), POOR=SS_EXT_PEELING or widespread failure (1.6x prep). Foundation prep modifiers are lower than masonry wall RP because foundation is small scope at ground level.

relevant_findings.topic: Efflorescence is the PRIMARY RP concern on foundation — ground contact drives salt migration
relevant_findings.finding: Foundation walls have continuous ground contact making them highly susceptible to efflorescence (salt migration through concrete). In RP context, existing coating may trap salts causing osmotic blistering — the #1 coating failure mode on foundation. Dormant efflorescence can be treated (dry brush, TSP wash, rinse). Active/recurring efflorescence = STOP WORK — moisture source not resolved. Treatment is a separate task from general prep wash.

relevant_findings.topic: Exposed bare masonry in RP requires alkali-resistant primer — pH 12-14
relevant_findings.finding: When existing coating fails on foundation and pressure washing/scraping exposes bare concrete or CMU, the surface is at pH 12-14. Alkali-resistant primer (SW Loxon Masonry Primer or equivalent) is MANDATORY on all exposed bare areas. In RP, this is spot prime on failure points — not full surface unless extensive peeling. Oil-based products remain PROHIBITED (saponification).

relevant_findings.topic: Block filler NOT applicable in RP — already applied during NC
relevant_findings.finding: CMU block filler (PCA P12 Level 2) is a substrate preparation step applied during new construction. In RP context, block filler is already in place. The existing filler provides a smooth base for recoating. If block filler is failing (unlikely — it is a cementitious material bonded to block), the scope is beyond painting — refer to masonry trade.

relevant_findings.topic: Foundation RP is ground-level only — no access modifier
relevant_findings.finding: Foundation band is at grade by definition (12-36 inches above grade). No ladder, scaffold, or lift needed. FAC_EXT_ACCESS is NOT applicable. This is the simplest access profile of any exterior spec. Walkout basements with exposed foundation above 3 ft are an edge case not modeled in v1.

relevant_findings.topic: Application methods for foundation RP: brush_roll primary, spray_backroll for larger runs
relevant_findings.finding: Foundation is typically a small-area scope. brush_roll is the primary method (brush for detail, roller for field). spray_backroll is available for larger continuous foundation runs (e.g., walkout basements). Spray-only remains valid on smooth poured concrete per NC research (no backroll needed for cosmetic coating on non-porous primed surface). CMU with spray SHOULD include backroll per masonry doctrine. Unlike masonry wall RP, foundation RP does NOT prohibit spray-only on poured concrete.

relevant_findings.topic: Coating systems: acrylic and cementitious (same as NC)
relevant_findings.finding: RP uses the same two coating systems as NC: acrylic (100% acrylic masonry paint) and cementitious (Drylok-type). Elastomeric is excluded (overkill for above-grade cosmetic coating). If previous coating was cementitious and is sound, recoat with cementitious. If previous coating was acrylic and is sound, recoat with acrylic. Cross-system recoating (acrylic over cementitious or vice versa) is acceptable with proper adhesion verification.

relevant_findings.topic: Foundation RP does NOT include lead-safe RRP
relevant_findings.finding: Foundation coating is a post-1978 practice (foundation walls were historically left bare). Pre-1978 homes with painted foundation are extremely rare. RRP module is excluded from foundation RP to keep it as the simplest exterior RP spec. If lead paint is suspected on a foundation, the project should be referred to lead abatement specialist.

relevant_findings.topic: Previous incorrect caulking at grade-line gap — RP-specific assessment task
relevant_findings.finding: In RP context, a previous painter may have incorrectly caulked the siding-to-foundation gap. Assessment must check for this. If caulked, the existing caulk must be removed and the gap restored as a drainage plane. This is a new RP-specific assessment task not present in NC.

relevant_findings.topic: Condition scale modifiers are lower for foundation than masonry wall
relevant_findings.finding: Foundation is small scope at ground level with simple geometry. Prep work is less complex than masonry wall. Condition scale modifiers: GOOD=1.0x, FAIR=1.3x, POOR=1.6x (vs masonry wall GOOD=1.0, FAIR=1.5, POOR=2.0). The reduced modifier range reflects: (1) smaller area means less total additional time, (2) ground-level access eliminates repositioning overhead that inflates masonry wall prep, (3) simpler geometry means less detail work in damaged areas.
relevant_findings.source: Engineering judgment calibrated from SF_MASONRY_EXT_RP_v1 condition modifiers

key_decisions.decision: QT2-QT3 only, matching NC spec. Foundation is utilitarian — QT4/QT5 excluded.
key_decisions.rationale: Foundation band is not a decorative surface. Even in RP, no homeowner requests premium treatment on foundation wall.

key_decisions.decision: RRP excluded. Foundation coating is a modern practice. Pre-1978 painted foundations are exceptionally rare.
key_decisions.rationale: Including RRP would add 5 tasks and complexity for a near-zero probability scenario. If encountered, refer to lead specialist.

key_decisions.decision: Block filler excluded from RP. Already applied during NC.
key_decisions.rationale: Block filler is a one-time substrate preparation. If filler is failing, the scope is masonry repair, not painting.

key_decisions.topic: Condition scale modifiers reduced from masonry wall RP
key_decisions.rationale: Ground-level access, small area, simple geometry reduce overhead that inflates masonry wall prep time.

key_decisions.decision: brush_roll is primary (small foundation areas). spray_backroll available for larger runs. Spray-only on poured concrete remains valid per NC research.
key_decisions.rationale: Foundation is typically small scope. Spray justification requires enough area to amortize equipment setup.

key_decisions.decision: Add TSK_FNRP_ASSESS_GRADE_GAP to check for incorrect caulking of the siding-to-foundation gap.
key_decisions.rationale: Previous painter may have caulked the drainage gap. Must assess and flag for removal. Not present in NC because new construction has clean gap.
